papers.title_en: ActionRoPE: Action as Coordinates for Spatially Consistent Control in Planar-Camera Game World Models
papers.authors: Zhiyang Deng, Yuzhe Wu, Zijun Lin, Yeying Jin
papers.evidence: 交互式游戏世界模型中的空间一致动作控制
papers.tldr: 平面相机游戏世界模型常用特征条件控制动作，难以保证空间一致。ActionRoPE将动作驱动的相机位移转换为世界坐标旋转位置，使同一世界位置在时间上保持相同位置地址。作者进一步提出CNS，按已观测与新增区域分配逐token去噪调度。实验表明该方法更忠实跟随指令运动，重访漂移较最强基线降低66%，并可跨1.3B至33B视频骨干和分布外场景迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world. This formulation is poorly matched to a broad class of planar-camera worlds, such as top-down and isometric games. In these worlds, player motion induces a geometrically well-defined planar camera displacement. We observe that the key to spatially consistent control in such worlds is to represent the effect of each action directly in world coordinates. To this end, we introduce ActionRoPE, a parameter-free action interface that converts action-driven camera displacement into world-coordinate rotary positions. As a result, tokens corresponding to the same world location retain the same positional address across time. These world coordinates further expose a spatial asymmetry in generation: regions covered by the initial observation are geometrically known, while newly revealed regions remain to be synthesized. We therefore propose Coordinate-Conditioned Noise Scheduling (CNS), which assigns token-wise denoising schedules according to this known-new structure. It allows observed regions to stabilize earlier, while new content is generated with reference to them. Compared with four representative action-conditioning mechanisms, our approach follows the commanded motion more faithfully and reduces the revisit drift by 66% over the strongest baseline. The same interface transfers across video backbones from 1.3B to 33B parameters and to out-of-distribution scenes. Project Page: https://teawhite.cn/ActionRoPE/.

papers.title_en: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
papers.authors: Shengqiong Wu, Meng Luo, Bobo Li, Ziwei Liu, Shuicheng Yan, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Philip Torr, Hao Fei
papers.evidence: 以世界建模统一视角综述视频理解与生成
papers.tldr: 视频基础模型与视频世界模型目标不同，却都关注视频观察与演化世界的关系。该综述以世界建模为统一视角，将观测视频视为潜在时序世界的部分、有损且有序投影，并围绕读、写、共享、交互四类操作梳理任务、表示、模型、数据与基准。文章强调应区分序列时序连贯与底层世界状态一致，指出研究正从片段识别和感知保真转向持久状态、可控演化、物理因果有效性与交互评估，并提炼开放挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.
